description.narrative: Lam Thuong, a newly merged mountainous commune in northern Vietnam, is endowed with pristine landscapes and rich cultural heritage of ethnic minority groups, primarily Tay and Dao. Yet local livelihoods remain dependent on small-scale agriculture that isincreasingly vulnerable to climate change. Women carry the majority of agricultural and domestic work but have limited access to training, income opportunities, and leadership roles. Emerging community-based tourism is spontaneous and unregulated, posingrisks to cultural integrity and the environment. In response, ECODE proposes the initiative “Lam Thuong – Heritage Revival, Green Livelihood Connection,” which aims to develop a women-led, climate-resilient, and culturally grounded community-based tourismmodel. The initiative alignsclosely with Oxfam’s priorities on green economic transition, women’s economic empowerment, and climate resilience. The initiative pursues three objectives: (1) Revitalize and document intangible cultural heritage throughcommunity-led preservation and digitalization; (2) Enhance the capacity, agency, and leadership of ethnic minority women to participate in and benefit from green livelihood opportunities; (3) Support local authorities to develop a Green Community-BasedTourism Development Plan integrated into the commune’ssocio-economic development planning (2026–2030). Key activities include establishing a women-led Cultural Heritage Club; digitizingcultural practices; training women and youth in community tourism,digital communication, climate adaptation, and green livelihood skills; supporting homestay improvements based on green criteria; strengthening the local tourism service cooperative; and facilitating policy consultations to embed green tourism into localplanning. The initiative will be implemented across all 31 villages of Lam Thuong Commune and will directly benefit 120–130 people, including at least 70 ethnic minority women, 30–35 young workers, and 20 households practicing community tourism. By placing women at the center of green transition, the initiative seeks to build a sustainable, inclusive, and culturally vibrant community-based tourism model that can serve as a replicable pathway for poverty reduction andclimate-resilient development in ethnic minority areas of Vietnam.

participating-org.narrative: The Center for Eco-Community Development (ECODE) is a non-profit organization established in 2015 under the Vietnam Union of Science and Technology Associations (VUSTA), as per Decision No. 685/QD-LHHVN. The main areas of expertise include climate change, adaptation and disaster risk management, nature conservation, environmental protection, and adaptive livelihood development. Over the years, ECODE has participated in and chaired several activities and Research and Development (R<(>&<)>D) projects associatedwith community development, especially supporting capacity building and promoting livelihood practices, responding to climate change for vulnerable communities, ethnic minorities, with a focus on ethnic minority women, and integrating gender. The goal isto contribute to enhancing the adaptive capacity of livelihoods and improving people's capacity and lives in the context of climate change associated with the conservation of nature, traditional culture, and the ecological environment.
